audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Kennen levels 4-5, first item and 2+ items while the whys attached to those exact rows say 'Sett owns this window', 'Sett reclaims this' and 'It stays even'. Levels 1-2 were scored Skill while the text says he is chipped for free.
audit.why: 50.54% over 368 games is a true coin flip that swings by stage: Kennen owns 1-2 on range, Sett owns 4-5 on the grab and the first-item Grit window, and it settles even after that.
audit.corrected: Chart re-sided to the packet in matched pairs: Kennen / Kennen / Skill / Sett / Skill / Sett / Skill. diffRating 4/10 -> 5/10 and tone moved off the favoured green.

audit.whatIsWrong: First item was written as Kennen's Liandry's spike ('force fights the moment it completes').
audit.why: The content layer already identifies first item as Sett's window — Grit-bruiser items out-sustain your burst once he lives through the stun. The full layer contradicted it.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why rewritten to Sett's Grit window; phases[3] and phases[6] aligned to the same reading.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two claims: Facebreaker described as a flat 'grab-stun', and The Show Stopper described as a 'suppress-slam' that 'interrupts your channel'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Facebreaker pulls in enemies on opposite sides and stuns them; if enemies were only on one side they are slowed instead. Against a lone Kennen it is a slow, and it only stuns when a minion or ally is on his far side. The Show Stopper carries a champion and slams them — it is a 400-range displacement, and nothing in Kennen's kit marks Slicing Maelstrom as a channel, so 'interrupts the channel' is not supportable. What it actually does is throw you clear of your own 550-radius storm.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker stated with its opposite-sides condition and 490 range; Show Stopper stated as a displacement out of your storm.
sources: ownerKit R range 550 and flags (no channel flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states that Haymaker's shield is charged by the damage you deal him.
audit.why: Sett passively stores damage taken as Grit and spends it all on cast for a shield plus true damage. Poking him with no intent to commit literally builds the tool that beats your all-in — the shield eats your burst window.
audit.corrected: Stated in dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d: your poke becomes Grit, so force W out before you commit.

audit.why: Haymaker at 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 and Facebreaker at 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 are both long enough to trade around, and the page already keys commits to them.

edits.before: Sett has no dash and no early waveclear, so your Thundering Shuriken plus Electrical Surge on-hit just chips him for free at levels 1-2 — last-hit at Q range and refuse to walk into E-grab distance. He wants to charge Haymaker (W) off your poke and your minion aggro, so trade in short bursts and step out before his bar fills. Do not facecheck or sidestep into his E line — a single grab into Knuckle Down is how he flips this lane.
edits.after: Sett has no dash and no early waveclear, so your Thundering Shuriken plus Electrical Surge on-hit chips him for free at levels 1-2 — last-hit at 950 and refuse to walk inside Facebreaker's 490. Every point of poke he eats is stored as Grit for Haymaker's shield, so trade in bursts and step out before the bar fills. Never let a minion sit on his far side: enemies on both sides of him turn the pull from a slow into a stun.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his window, not yours: he hits his level-3 combo (E grab into W true-damage smash) and your fragile body can't survive a clean grab the way a bruiser can. Keep building Mark of the Storm from range and only commit the third-stack stun when his E is down. At 6 it's a coin flip — your R stacks marks and stun-locks, but his R suppress-slam cancels your Maelstrom channel and your Lightning Rush engage, so don't burn ult into an up grab-and-slam.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his window, not yours: Facebreaker into a full-Grit Haymaker smash kills a fragile body a bruiser would survive. Keep building Mark of the Storm from range and commit the third-stack stun only while that 16s E is down. At 6 it's a coin flip — your R stacks marks and stun-locks, but The Show Stopper carries you 400 units clear of your own storm, so don't burn ult while his grab-and-slam is up. Hold it for the fight after.

edits.after: Bait your E-in, then Show Stopper you clear of your own storm

notes: Two mechanical corrections drive this file. (1) Facebreaker only stuns when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett — against a lone Kennen it is a slow — and the page asserted a flat grab-stun in three places. (2) The Show Stopper was called a 'suppress-slam' that 'interrupts your channel'; Riot's text describes a carry-and-slam, and Kennen's kit carries no channel flag on Slicing Maelstrom, so the real effect stated is a 400-range displacement out of your own 550 storm. Also added the missing shield-absorbs-burst interaction: Sett's Grit is charged by your own poke. Note for the user: the brief's top-level games field says 869 while packet.games says 368 — I used 368/50.54% since that is the pair the packet reports together.
